campaign.description: The invitation campaign the visitor arrived with — `InviteCode.campaign`, the free-text tag the generation CLI stamps on a batch of codes (SUP-142). This is the join key between the two tools and the database; omitted when the visit carried no code.

has_invite.description: Whether the request carried an `?invite=` code (or the `cr_invite` cookie the landing set from one). Always present, so `false` is a countable population rather than a gap.

utm_source.description: `utm_source` as it arrived in the URL, lower-cased and trimmed. Landing only.

utm_medium.description: `utm_medium` as it arrived in the URL, lower-cased and trimmed. Landing only.

utm_campaign.description: `utm_campaign` as it arrived in the URL, lower-cased and trimmed. Usually equal to `campaign`, but it is the marketer's string, not ours, so the two are recorded separately.

utm_content.description: `utm_content` as it arrived in the URL, lower-cased and trimmed — which variant of the mail the click came from.

position.description: Which part of the page the element sits in. A closed set: it is the breakdown the copy decisions are made from, so a new section adds a value here in the same change.

outcome.description: Whether the server-side action credited the account or declined to.

grant_micros.description: Micro-USD credited, integer, per the money convention in ADR-005 ($100 is 100000000). Present only when `outcome` is `granted`.

events.name: landing_view
events.when: The landing page is loaded at router.superprotocol.com. This is Plausible's automatic pageview, not a second custom event.
events.notes: The name is the taxonomy's; in Plausible's UI the row reads `pageview`. The properties below ride it through the `pageview-props` script variant, so no extra request is made and the page is never double-counted.

events.name: cta_click
events.when: A primary call-to-action is activated (click, or Enter/Space on the focused control) — before the navigation, with Plausible's own queueing so the beacon survives the unload.
events.notes: `target: signup` is the landing half of the funnel: it is the last thing we can observe before the browser leaves for the console, which is a different origin with no shared identifier. Register it as a Plausible goal.

target.description: Where the call-to-action sends the visitor.

events.name: diagram_variant_shown
events.when: The how-it-works diagram first enters the viewport, once per page load, reporting the variant the CSS actually resolved to.
events.notes: The artboard ships two diagrams and the breakpoint decides; this is how we learn which one most visitors were shown before judging the section's engagement.

variant.description: Which of the artboard's two diagrams is rendered at this width.

viewport_bucket.description: Coarse width bucket at the moment the diagram appeared: mobile <768, tablet <1024, desktop <1440, wide otherwise. Buckets, not pixels — a pixel width is a high-cardinality property and a weak fingerprinting signal.

events.name: code_copied
events.when: A copy button on a code sample succeeds (the clipboard write resolved), or the sample is copied with the keyboard from inside its container.

snippet.description: Which sample was copied. The closed set is the samples the page ships; adding a sample adds a value.

events.name: faq_opened
events.when: An FAQ item is expanded. Collapsing it again sends nothing.

question_id.description: The FAQ item's stable slug — the id already used as the disclosure's anchor, not the question text, so re-wording a question does not start a new series.

events.name: docs_link_click
events.when: An outbound link to documentation or to another Super Protocol property is activated.
events.notes: Plausible's outbound-link extension would report these as `Outbound Link: Click` with the raw URL; we send our own named event instead so the breakdown is a handful of destinations rather than one row per URL.

destination.description: Which property the link leads to. Closed set: an unrecognised host is not sent at all rather than widening the breakdown.

events.name: signup_started
events.when: The sign-up screen is presented on console.router.superprotocol.com, once per page load.
events.notes: Anonymous and deliberately unstitched: it is captured with `$process_person_profile: false` and a per-request random `distinct_id`, because linking it to the account that appears later would need an identifier stored in the visitor's browser — the thing ADR-006 §4 rules out. Read it as a volume, and read the landing → account edge from `cta_click{target: signup}`, from `invite_redeemed`, and from `inviteCampaignStats`.

entry.description: How the visitor reached the screen, from the URL alone: `landing_cta` when the invite or UTM parameters are present, `invite_link` when an invitation URL was opened directly at the console, `login_switch` from the sign-in screen's link, `direct` otherwise.

events.name: signup_completed
events.when: router-api's account-creation hook has committed — the same `user.create.after` boundary the invitation grant runs in (SUP-142) — so the event exists only for accounts that exist.
events.notes: The first identified event: `distinct_id` is the account's UUID. No email, no name, no IP is sent as a person property (ADR-006 §4). Idempotency `uuid` is derived from the user id, so a retried hook cannot double-count a sign-up.

method.description: Which of ADR-004's three paths created the account.

events.name: invite_redeemed
events.when: The redemption attempt inside sign-up resolves — for every attempt that carried a code, whether it credited the account or was declined. A sign-up with no code sends nothing.
events.notes: Refusals are the point: a campaign whose codes were all spent before the mail went out looks identical to a campaign nobody opened unless the refusal reason is recorded. Idempotency `uuid` is the `InviteRedemption` row id. `reason` mirrors `InviteRedemptionOutcome` in router-api.

reason.description: Why the code was declined. Present only when `outcome` is `refused`.

events.name: api_key_created
events.when: The `createApiKey` mutation has committed. The key's own value and label are never part of the event.

has_spend_limit.description: Whether the key was created with a per-key spend limit.

keys_after.description: How many live keys the workspace has after this one — the cheap way to separate the first key (an activation step) from the tenth (an integration habit).

events.name: first_request_sent
events.when: A workspace's first generation reaches a terminal state, exactly once per workspace, decided by the workspace's own first-request timestamp inside the recording transaction rather than by a count.
events.notes: The event the whole campaign is judged on: an account that redeemed $100 and never sent a token did not convert. `inviteCampaignStats.activated` answers the same question from the database and is the number to trust when the two disagree.

model_slug.description: The catalogue slug of the model the first request went to — a closed set in practice, since it can only be a model the router serves.

hours_since_signup.description: Whole hours between account creation and this request, floored. Hours rather than a timestamp difference computed in the tool, so the number survives export.

had_invite_grant.description: Whether this workspace's ledger holds an invitation grant — the split that says whether the $100 did anything.

events.name: model_requested
events.when: The `requestModel` mutation has committed a row.
events.notes: The requested model name and any note stay in our database, where SUP-146's admin aggregation and CSV export read them. They are not event properties: free text is a breakdown with one row per request, and it is the one field on either surface where a visitor could type something personal.

source.description: Which screen the request was raised from.

has_details.description: Whether the requester wrote anything in the free-text field — how much the field earns its place, without reading it.

events.name: feedback_form_opened
events.when: The feedback form is opened from the console — the click, not the form provider's own view event.
events.notes: Identified: the console posts it to router-api on the session, so `distinct_id` is the account's UUID and the form provider needs no identifier of ours in its URL.

source.description: Where the invitation to give feedback was shown.

grant_eligible.description: Whether this account could still earn the second grant at the moment it opened the form.

events.name: feedback_grant_applied
events.when: The signed form webhook has been verified and the second grant resolved, whether it credited the account or was declined.
events.notes: Idempotency `uuid` is the ledger entry id (or the webhook delivery id on a refusal), so a provider redelivery cannot show as two grants. No answer text is ever sent.

reason.description: Why the second grant was declined. Present only when `outcome` is `refused`.
